The Hebrew has a singular fishing spear for his head; BSB has fishing spears.
The Hebrew commands laying a hand on him and not repeating the battle; BSB frames laying a hand as a condition.
The Hebrew names his hope without explicitly supplying overcoming him; BSB adds that description.
The Hebrew leaves the animal unnamed here; BSB explicitly names Leviathan.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew wording here affirms keeping silent, with no explicit negative; BSB says I cannot keep silent.
The Hebrew names doubled bridle or halter; BSB says a bridle without doubled.
The Hebrew names doors of his face; BSB names jaws.
The Hebrew names shields; BSB calls them scales.
The Hebrew does not explicitly repeat scale; BSB supplies it.
The Hebrew describes each joined to its brother; BSB says one another.
The Hebrew names sneezing and the eyelids of dawn; BSB says snorting and rays of dawn.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names a fanned pot and reeds without an explicit burning; BSB describes a boiling pot over burning reeds.
The Hebrew has a singular flame; BSB has flames.

The Hebrew names his heart as cast like stone; BSB describes his chest as hard as rock.
The Hebrew uses wording of purifying themselves at the crashes; BSB describes withdrawing before his thrashing.
The Hebrew says the sword does not stand; BSB says it has no effect.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the arrow a son of a bow; BSB simply says arrow.
The Hebrew uses a plural passive verb with club and describes shaking the javelin; BSB uses a singular passive clause and names the sound of the lance.
The Hebrew describes spreading a threshing sledge over mud; BSB describes spreading out mud like a threshing sledge.
